newsitem.title: USA: Enron out of the bidding for German utility.
newsitem.headline: Enron out of the bidding for German utility.

text.p: U.S. power marketer Enron Corp has dropped out of the bidding for German state utility group Berliner Kraft und Licht AG, or Bewag, a spokesman with the Houston company said on Wednesday.

"After careful evaluation, we have decided not to pursue the purchase of shares in Bewag at this point in time," the spokesman said. "However, we remain interested in the German energy market and continue to look for opportunities to participate as it deregulates and moves toward a new era of competition."

U.S. companies Enron and Southern Co were among a group of foreign firms eyeing acquisition of the Berlin government's stake in Bewag. The government said it is seeking to sell at least 25.8 percent of its 50.8 percent stake in the utility by the end of February.

Atlanta-based Southern is still mulling a possible offer for Bewag, but has not made a formal bid for the Berlin utility, a spokesman told Reuters. "We are one of a number of people looking into that property," spokesman Dave Mould said. "We have not reached a final decision on a bid."
